lines.text: Grab four socks from a drawer of five pairs. How often do you get a matching pair?
lines.caption: Grab four socks from a drawer of five pairs. How often do you get a matching pair?

lines.text: Counting the matches head-on gets messy. Counting the NON-matches is much easier.
lines.caption: Counting the matches head-on gets messy. Counting the NON-matches is much easier.

lines.text: Hello, I'm Vantee, and today we're sorting socks!
lines.caption: Hello, I'm Vantee, and today we're sorting socks!

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A drawer has five pairs of socks, and each pair is a different color.
lines.caption: A drawer has five pairs of socks, and each pair is a different color.

lines.text: Zoe pulls out four socks.
lines.caption: Zoe pulls out four socks.

lines.text: How many sets of four socks contain at least one matching pair?
lines.caption: How many sets of four socks contain at least one matching pair?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we know? Ten socks in all, two of each color. Each sock is its own sock.
lines.caption: So what do we know? Ten socks in all, two of each color. Each sock is its own sock.

lines.text: A set of four is just which socks she holds. The order doesn't matter.
lines.caption: A set of four is just which socks she holds. The order doesn't matter.

lines.text: At least one pair means one matching pair, or even two pairs. Both count.
lines.caption: At least one pair means one matching pair, or even two pairs. Both count.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: count everything, then take away the sets with no pair.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: count everything, then take away the sets with no pair.

lines.text: All sets minus no-pair sets leaves the sets with a pair.
lines.caption: All sets minus no-pair sets leaves the sets with a pair.

lines.text: First, all sets. Pick socks one at a time: ten choices, then nine, then eight, then seven.
lines.caption: First, all sets. Pick socks one at a time: ten choices, then nine, then eight, then seven.

lines.text: That's five thousand forty.
lines.caption: That's five thousand forty.

lines.text: But each set got counted once for every order.
lines.caption: But each set got counted once for every order.

lines.text: Four socks can line up in four times three times two times one, twenty-four orders.
lines.caption: Four socks can line up in four times three times two times one, twenty-four orders.

lines.text: So five thousand forty divided by twenty-four is two hundred ten sets in all.
lines.caption: So five thousand forty divided by twenty-four is two hundred ten sets in all.

lines.text: Now the no-pair sets. No pair means four different colors.
lines.caption: Now the no-pair sets. No pair means four different colors.

lines.text: Choose four of the five colors. That's the same as choosing the one color to leave out: five ways.
lines.caption: Choose four of the five colors. That's the same as choosing the one color to leave out: five ways.

lines.text: Each chosen color has two socks to pick from. Two times two times two times two is sixteen.
lines.caption: Each chosen color has two socks to pick from. Two times two times two times two is sixteen.

lines.text: So there are five times sixteen, eighty sets with no pair.
lines.caption: So there are five times sixteen, eighty sets with no pair.

lines.text: Two hundred ten minus eighty is one hundred thirty.
lines.caption: Two hundred ten minus eighty is one hundred thirty.

lines.text: One hundred thirty sets have a pair. That's Choice C!
lines.caption: One hundred thirty sets have a pair. That's Choice C!

lines.text: Here's another way. Let's count the sets with a pair directly, in two groups.
lines.caption: Here's another way. Let's count the sets with a pair directly, in two groups.

lines.text: Exactly one pair: five colors for the pair.
lines.caption: Exactly one pair: five colors for the pair.

lines.text: Then two different colors from the other four, six ways, and a sock of each, four ways.
lines.caption: Then two different colors from the other four, six ways, and a sock of each, four ways.

lines.text: Five times six times four is one hundred twenty.
lines.caption: Five times six times four is one hundred twenty.

lines.text: Two pairs: choose two of the five colors. There are ten ways.
lines.caption: Two pairs: choose two of the five colors. There are ten ways.

lines.text: One hundred twenty plus ten is one hundred thirty. Same answer!
lines.caption: One hundred twenty plus ten is one hundred thirty. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? It's a great double-check. But the first way didn't need to split into cases.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? It's a great double-check. But the first way didn't need to split into cases.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice A says eighty. That's the sets with NO pair, the group we took away.
lines.caption: Choice A says eighty. That's the sets with NO pair, the group we took away.

lines.text: Choice E, two hundred ten, is every set, before taking any away.
lines.caption: Choice E, two hundred ten, is every set, before taking any away.

lines.text: Choice D, one hundred forty, comes from picking a pair, five ways.
lines.caption: Choice D, one hundred forty, comes from picking a pair, five ways.

lines.text: Then any two of the other eight socks: eight times seven over two, twenty-eight ways. Five times twenty-eight is one hundred forty.
lines.caption: Then any two of the other eight socks: eight times seven over two, twenty-eight ways. Five times twenty-eight is one hundred forty.

lines.text: But a two-pair set gets counted twice, once for each pair.
lines.caption: But a two-pair set gets counted twice, once for each pair.

lines.text: Take away the ten extras, and you're back to one hundred thirty.
lines.caption: Take away the ten extras, and you're back to one hundred thirty.

lines.text: Choice B, one hundred twenty-five, doesn't come from any correct count. Both our methods give one hundred thirty.
lines.caption: Choice B, one hundred twenty-five, doesn't come from any correct count. Both our methods give one hundred thirty.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. For at least one, count the opposite and subtract.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. For at least one, count the opposite and subtract.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now the drawer has six pairs, each a different color.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Now the drawer has six pairs, each a different color.

lines.text: Zoe pulls out four socks again. How many sets of four contain at least one matching pair?
lines.caption: Zoe pulls out four socks again. How many sets of four contain at least one matching pair?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Count every set: twelve times eleven times ten times nine, divided by twenty-four.
lines.caption: Let's check. Count every set: twelve times eleven times ten times nine, divided by twenty-four.

lines.text: That's four hundred ninety-five.
lines.caption: That's four hundred ninety-five.

lines.text: No pair: choose four of the six colors.
lines.caption: No pair: choose four of the six colors.

lines.text: That's the same as leaving out two colors: six times five over two, fifteen ways. Then sixteen ways to pick the socks.
lines.caption: That's the same as leaving out two colors: six times five over two, fifteen ways. Then sixteen ways to pick the socks.

lines.text: Fifteen times sixteen is two hundred forty sets with no pair.
lines.caption: Fifteen times sixteen is two hundred forty sets with no pair.

lines.text: Four hundred ninety-five minus two hundred forty is two hundred fifty-five!
lines.caption: Four hundred ninety-five minus two hundred forty is two hundred fifty-five!

lines.text: Check: one pair gives six times ten times four, two hundred forty, and two pairs gives six times five over two, fifteen.
lines.caption: Check: one pair gives six times ten times four, two hundred forty, and two pairs gives six times five over two, fifteen.

lines.text: Two hundred fifty-five again!
lines.caption: Two hundred fifty-five again!

lines.text: If you got two hundred fifty-five, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you got two hundred fifty-five, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: When a question says at least one, count the opposite.
lines.caption: When a question says at least one, count the opposite.

lines.text: Count all the sets, subtract the ones with none, and what's left is your answer.
lines.caption: Count all the sets, subtract the ones with none, and what's left is your answer.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
